feed.title: Stapledon's Voyage news
feed.subtitle: Releases and progress on Stapledon's Voyage, a hard-SF game in Godot 4 and AILANG.

entry.title: Manual sky exposure and a one-AU arrival: v0.4.0-dev.14
entry.summary: The painted ship and Solar departure tour share one perspective. This review build removes automatic sky dimming: exposure stays at your manually selected brightness while you move and look around. The tour finishes one AU from Alpha Centauri A.
entry.content:
The painted ship and Solar departure tour share one perspective. This review build removes automatic sky dimming: exposure stays at your manually selected brightness while you move and look around. The tour finishes one AU from Alpha Centauri A.

Development build: macOS only (Apple Silicon)v0.4.0-dev.14-manual-sky

Painted ship and Solar departure tour

Download for macOS

Pre-alpha and unsigned. After unzipping, clear the quarantine flag once:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "Stapledons Voyage.app"

What's new​

  • One current painted ship: seven major tiers, a bridge floor and captain shadow that meet the walking surface, faster movement, trackpad look and known-star inspection. Integration PR.
  • Gradual approaches: the guided tour uses physical 1 g acceleration with 90 seconds of braking playback. Earth, Jupiter and Saturn sit beside the bridge at their close stops. Ordinary navigation keeps its existing pacing. Integration PR.
  • Manual sky exposure: J cycles the brightness settings, also available under Tab. Bright planets and suns can wash out at a setting chosen for stars; camera pans and journeys no longer change exposure automatically. The physical light and SR calculations remain unchanged.
  • Smoother tour starts: initialize the camera from the new session and ease departure time compression over three seconds. This corrects an initial camera jump and an abrupt first movement beside Earth.
  • Measured stars: Alpha Centauri A/B use measured radii and temperatures; the final leg intercepts the moving primary at 1 AU. A's disc is about 0.65° wide there. Integration PR.
  • Review evidence: the gallery and geometry reference include fresh native captures and editable Blender masters. B keeps the full benchmark locally and attempts an authenticated upload of filtered aggregate measurements. Integration PR.

Not yet​

Ship lighting is still an internal lighting study; external sunlight, detailed moon surfaces and further Commons art remain in progress. Fresh M2 Air performance needs a laptop measurement. Tour stops are inertial clearance stops: gravity, thermal hazards and GR are not simulated. Stellar photospheres are uniform emitters.

Release: v0.4.0-dev.14-manual-sky · Gallery · Ship reference.

entry.title: Walkable bridge demo: v0.4.0-dev.1
entry.summary: A development build you can download: walk the captain around the bridge under the live
entry.content:
A development build you can download: walk the captain around the bridge under the live relativistic sky, open the galaxy map from the nav console, and fly a journey to α Centauri A through the bubble. macOS only, Apple Silicon.

Development build: macOS only (Apple Silicon)v0.4.0-dev.14-manual-sky

Painted ship and Solar departure tour

Download for macOS

Pre-alpha and unsigned. After unzipping, clear the quarantine flag once:

xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine "Stapledons Voyage.app"

What's new​

  • The walkable bridge (M4.2, #102): the bridge disc at the top of the spire, composited with the live sky through the same camera. The captain walks it (WASD, E to use) and ages with ship time.
  • Navigation from the bridge: a nav console opens the galaxy map (M), built from the real catalogues: 5,685 stars within 25 pc, companions at their system's distance. Commit to α Centauri A and watch the boost, the 0.99c cruise, the brake and the arrival.
  • The relativistic sky behind it all: 335k real stars, aberration and Doppler colour, the naked-eye exposure, and the forward glow of the cosmic background at extreme speed.
  • L opens the log and K the codex.

Not yet​

  • The forward bubble-wall glow is off; it returns with the next simulation step.
  • The standalone sky flight (-- --voyage) shows a mirrored sky in this build: fixed on main (#107), in the next build. The view from the bridge is correct.
  • The bridge is v1 demo art; the final art is in progress (concept art).
  • Pre-alpha and unsigned; see Try it for install notes.

Release: v0.4.0-dev.1 (macOS development build)

entry.title: Concept art: the captain and the bridge
entry.summary: The ship has faces now. The captain is picked, the crew have proposed portraits, and the bridge
entry.content:
The ship has faces now. The captain is picked, the crew have proposed portraits, and the bridge stands in the engine over the live sky.

What's new​

  • The captain, the Longline Navigator (#98): picked from three silhouette proposals, and drawn front and back at 30, 50, 70 and 90, because the game spans a 100-year career.
  • Crew cast proposals: one portrait per role, next to the Medic's accepted set.
  • Bridge v1 (#97, demo art): the first real interior, a disc at the top of the spire inside the sphere ship. The sky behind the railings is not painted; it is the game's live sky, through the same camera, so at 0.99c it crowds forward and turns blue.

Not yet​

Bridge v1 is demo art. A v2 quality study is done and the final art is being made. Everything is on the concept art page, labelled with its status.

entry.title: Planets are coming
entry.summary: A new milestone, M5, brings planets, moons and flybys inside a star system, with the same rule as
entry.content:
A new milestone, M5, brings planets, moons and flybys inside a star system, with the same rule as the sky: real data, real physics.

What's done​

  • The design and the sprint plan are approved (#84, #86).
  • A new AILANG package, sunholo/celestial 0.1.0, published with 93 tests: a Kepler solver, JPL planetary ephemerides for 3000 BC to 3000 AD plus moons, IAU reference frames, light-time, gravity, reflectance, and planetary rings.
  • sunholo/relativity 0.6 and 0.7: the bubble's forward glow, and the aberrated outline of a nearby sphere, which is what a planet looks like as you pass it near light speed.

What's planned​

Start held above Earth, pick a body on a system map (the Sun, 8 planets, 11 moons, 4 ring systems), choose to stop or fly by at 0.001c to 0.99c, commit, and ride the leg. The views will be exact: light-time delay, aberration, and the Terrell rotation that makes a passing sphere look turned. At α Centauri, the known and candidate planets will show as points only, with a badge saying how sure the astronomy is. The first step, the Sol and α Cen data and the game's package pins, has merged (#99).

See the roadmap.

entry.title: The ship's AI foundation
entry.summary: The crew's optional AI layer runs end to end, so far on a deterministic test stub: lines with
entry.content:
The crew's optional AI layer runs end to end, so far on a deterministic test stub: lines with emotion markers, portraits that change with them, a voice, and a hard cost ceiling.

What's new​

  • Emotion markers (AI.1–AI.3): a line carries markers like {loving}, validated before the game uses it.
  • A service the game never waits on (AI.4–AI.7): provider routing, a cache, a supervised background process, and key hygiene: a key never appears on a command line.
  • The Medic's accepted portraits, pinned and content-addressed (AI.8).
  • Opt-in and capped (AI.9): live AI stays off until the player adds a key and ticks the box. A ceiling the player sets (US$0.50 by default) stops spending, and automated runs can never go live.
  • The conversation scene (AI.10a, #91): the portrait cross-fades as each emotion marker arrives, the subtitles build segment by segment, and the voice plays.

Not yet​

No live model has been called. The first live run (AI.10b) is attended: one real line and a few voice auditions under a US$1 ceiling. The voice in the clip is a placeholder.

entry.title: A galaxy map from real catalogues
entry.summary: The galaxy map now draws from the same star catalogues as the sky, and stars that belong together
entry.content:
The galaxy map now draws from the same star catalogues as the sky, and stars that belong together stay together.

What's new​

  • The map on the catalogue tiers (#81): 5,687 stars within 25 pc, up from 3,802, with full-precision positions. α Centauri A and B are separate stars you can select.
  • Companion stars at their system's distance (#89): a companion within 60″ and 2,000 AU of its primary, agreeing in parallax and proper motion, takes the system's distance rather than its own noisier one. That moved 20,524 companions; Sirius B, for one, now sits with Sirius A at 8.6 ly.

Not yet​

Both are in the walkable bridge demo, v0.4.0-dev.1.

entry.title: The relativistic sky
entry.summary: The sky out of the window is now the real one: 335,157 stars over the Milky Way, exposed for a
entry.content:
The sky out of the window is now the real one: 335,157 stars over the Milky Way, exposed for a dark-adapted human eye, with the cosmic background glowing ahead at extreme speeds.

What's new​

  • Starfield v2 (#67): 335,157 stars from CNS5, Gaia GCNS and Hipparcos, instanced on the GPU, with float64 positions rebased around the ship.
  • The Milky Way behind them: the NOIRLab panorama with the catalogue's own stars removed, so stars are not counted twice, Doppler shifted texel by texel.
  • A naked-eye exposure (#75, #80): stars in lux and the sky in cd/m², calibrated so the faintest visible star lands at V 6.9 (Crumey's model says 6.897). The HUD always says how it is exposing; the readability aids are off by default and labelled.
  • The forward CMB glow (#79, fixed in #88): above γ ≈ 150 the 2.7 K microwave background, blueshifted, shows up dead ahead; at γ 707 it is a 3,853.7 K blackbody.

Not yet​

M1's acceptance step (M1.5b) is still open: the reference renders at five speeds and the 60 fps bench at 1440p with everything on. See the roadmap.

entry.title: v0.3: plan, commit, transit, arrive
entry.summary: The journey core is complete: pick a star, commit, watch both clocks run, and arrive. Once you
entry.content:
The journey core is complete: pick a star, commit, watch both clocks run, and arrive. Once you commit, there is no going back.

What's new​

  • Commit: hold for 1.5 s. After that the simulation refuses every cancel, and says so.
  • Transit and arrival: the phase, both clocks, the distance flown and the energy radiated, live, until you arrive.
  • Deterministic replay: a 10,000-tick session replays byte for byte on the AILANG VM and the interpreter.
  • v0.3.1 opens straight onto the galaxy map; v0.3.2 adds trackpad zoom and Retina scaling.

Not yet​

The interior of the ship, and a journey you live through on board, are the next milestone (M4).

Releases: v0.3.0, v0.3.1, v0.3.2 (macOS review builds)

entry.title: v0.2.0: a galaxy map with real numbers
entry.summary: The game now opens on a 3D map of the nearby stars. Click one and the simulation plans the trip:
entry.content:
The game now opens on a 3D map of the nearby stars. Click one and the simulation plans the trip: your years against Earth's.

What's new​

  • A galaxy map of the nearby-star catalogue: drag to orbit, scroll to zoom, click to plan.
  • A cruise slider from 0.9c to 0.999999c, spaced evenly in rapidity, 0.99c by default.
  • Every number on the panel comes straight from the AILANG simulation. α Centauri A at 0.99c: 0.6208 years for you, 4.401 for Earth, 1.80 minutes of boost at each end.

Not yet​

Committing to the journey and flying it came in the next build.

Release: v0.2.0-m2-map (macOS review build)

entry.title: v0.1.0: the spike
entry.summary: The first review build: an AILANG simulation driving a Godot starfield, with relativity that is
entry.content:
The first review build: an AILANG simulation driving a Godot starfield, with relativity that is tested rather than eyeballed.

What's new​

  • The simulation runs in AILANG as a child process, talking one line of JSON per tick with Godot (about 50 µs per round trip). It flies the ship at 1 g with exact rapidity kinematics.
  • The starfield: 3,802 nearby stars (CNS5), each aberrated toward the bow, coloured as a Doppler-shifted blackbody and beamed brighter ahead.
  • 27 physics reference checks, and 9 cases where the GPU shader must put a star where the CPU reference says, to under 0.1 px.

Not yet​

No Milky Way behind the stars, one axis of motion, and star colours from the spectral class only. All three were fixed in M1.

Release: v0.1.0-m0 (macOS review build)
